verses.author: model_A
verses.text: An orchard planted by a man who never tasted its fruit.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Someone else's laundry, drying stiff on my line—
I forgot whose turn it was to bring it in.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Rain starts again, no warning at all—
I still can't tell which window was left open

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The mail keeps coming for a name I don't recognize—
I sort it anyway, into piles that mean nothing

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Someone's shoes left by the door, too small for anyone here—
I step around them every morning, never asking

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
A crow keeps dropping stones on the roof at dawn—
I've started leaving something out for it

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The neighbor waves from her garden, mouth moving—
I nod like I've heard every word she's said

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The porch light burns through breakfast into noon—
I keep forgetting which of us was supposed to turn it off

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Rain fills the birdbath no bird visits—
I watch the surface shiver and call it company

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The mail slot clicks twice before I hear it—
I let the letters sit unopened on the mat

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The kettle screams until I lift it off the flame—
still I stand there, waiting for the quiet to answer back

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The neighbor's dog answers every siren for a mile—
I've stopped telling it there's nothing wrong

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The porch light hums on before the dark arrives—
I've learned to trust the bulb more than the sky

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The clock's second hand drags on the loudest days—
I count the drags instead of what they're counting toward

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The bread goes stale before I finish the loaf—
still I cut thin slices, calling it breakfast

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The mail slot clicks twice before the letter falls—
I've started guessing what it doesn't say
